r: Many rajas in an **assembly of clan heads**
8 clans – **Lichchhavis** (most powerful), Videhas, Jnatrikas, Vajjis; capital **Vaishali** = seat of the **world's first republic**; led by **Chetaka**, maternal uncle of **Mahavira**
Confederacy of 9 clans; capitals **Kushinara** (Buddha's **Mahaparinirvana**) and **Pava** (Mahavira died)
A monarchy in the 6th century BCE but a **sangha** in the Arthashastra
Also 16, some different names; adds Vanga, Malava, Ladha
Born at **Pushkalavati** (Gandhara); Ashtadhyayi = ~4,000 sutras in **8 chapters**
Anga, Magadha, Kashi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Shurasena, Ashmaka, Avanti, Gandhara, Kamboja

3.x: **Four great powers:** **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti**. After Magadha, **Kosala** (which absorbed Kashi and the Shakyas) was the strongest – "only Koshala and Magadha emerged as powerful".
**Kosala** annexed **Kashi**; Magadha later got it as dowry and by war. **Pradyota** rivalled **Bimbisara and Udayana**.

r: The Buddha visited **Kaushambi** in his reign
Turned Buddhist under **Pindola Bharadvaja**; donated the **Ghoshitarama** vihara
The **only Mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas**, on the **Godavari** (between the Godavari and Manjira); on the **Dakshinapatha**
**Potana / Potali = Bodhan, Nizamabad (Telangana)**; some place it at **Paithan (ancient Pratishthana)**
Sage **Bavari's** ashram on the Godavari in Assaka – earliest Andhra-region link in Buddhist texts
